newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Fuel stocks still low in some parts Germany - trade.
newsitem.headline: Fuel stocks still low in some parts Germany - trade.

text.p: Private stocks of heating oil in Germany rose from 61.9 to 65.0 percent of capacity during September, but the higher nationwide figure hid significant regional differences, said traders who have seen a confidential monthly report produced for the German oil industry.
Northern and southwestern regions were the slowest to prepare for winter, while stocks in the west along the Rhine stood above 1995, they said.
"Buying...was noticeably high in the middle of the country," said one.
At 65 percent capacity, levels for Germany as a whole were still six percent below September 1995 and five percent below the average over the past 15 years.
Traders said the shortfall was not as acute as at the end of the summer when levels were, on average, nine to 10 percent below last year.
"September was very good -- big quantities and good margins," one German supplier said.
"I bought a lot in the last month, although not so much very recently as the prices then really were too high," said another.
In the west, along much of the Rhine, consumer stocks increased from 60 to 68 percent of capacity, a level higher than in last year.

But in the north, inventories only edged up from 61 to 63 percent, still nine percent below September 1995. And in the southwest, principally in Bavaria, stocks stood at 64 percent, barely higher than August and 10 percent below last year.

"The end-users may not want to buy much more, but if they do buy, I guess the stock levels show that (gas oil) cargo demand into the north could still be high for a month or two," a Hamburg-based trader said.
